LESSON: RESPONSIBILITY OVER PLANTS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Creation 2.2 Stewardship over Creation (6 lessons) By the end of the sub- strand
Topic 2.3: Responsibility over Plants

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Responsibility over Plants. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should you take care of plants?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the biblical responsibilities given to human beings over plants
2. apply the biblical teachings acquired to conserve the environment
3. discuss how responsible use of plants contribute to economic growth

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: RESPONSIBILITY OVER PLANTS
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Responsibility over Plants helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT PLANTS
Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.
Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.
Without water and light, most seedlings wilt.

PART 1: Describe the biblical responsibilities given to human beings over plants

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the biblical responsibilities given to human beings over plants. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the biblical responsibilities given to human beings over plants.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Responsibility over Plants” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the biblical responsibilities given to human beings over plants. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply the biblical teachings acquired to conserve the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to apply the biblical teachings acquired to conserve the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply the biblical teachings acquired to conserve the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Responsibility over Plants matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply the biblical teachings acquired to conserve the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Discuss how responsible use of plants contribute to economic growth

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss how responsible use of plants contribute to economic growth. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss how responsible use of plants contribute to economic growth.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Responsibility over Plants this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss how responsible use of plants contribute to economic growth. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Responsibility over Plants is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.

Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Responsibility over Plants” around your school. (skill: describe the biblical responsibilities given to human beings over plants)

Example 2: Say why Responsibility over Plants matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: apply the biblical teachings acquired to conserve the environment)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Responsibility over Plants this week. (skill: discuss how responsible use of plants contribute to economic growth)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Responsibility over Plants to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the biblical responsibilities given to human beings over plants.
3. Practise this skill: apply the biblical teachings acquired to conserve the environment.
4. Practise this skill: discuss how responsible use of plants contribute to economic growth.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Responsibility over Plants from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Responsibility over Plants: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Responsibility over Plants?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should you take care of plants?
2. How do you care for plants in your environment?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Responsibility over Plants means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the biblical responsibilities given to human beings over plants.
5. Be able to: apply the biblical teachings acquired to conserve the environment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
